## Coordinator disposition and documented browser workflow

Create a **separately owned Linux Chromium process using the public Playwright launch and CDPSession APIs** solely for this profiling task. This document is the repository's specialized profiling workflow; T3 collaborative preview remains the gameplay/review browser. The change of environment answers the concrete unavailable trace capability. It is not a replacement triggered by a failed page open, nor permission to attach to T3's working shared browser.

Read `/work/repos/fleet/BROWSER_RULES.md` and `docs/BROWSER_RULES.md` before opening any browser. Verify factory-worker/isolated Linux, browser executable and actual owned process identity. Use a private profile/context and available port5191; never touch shared/human/peer tabs, process flags, storage, pipes or debugging endpoints. Read the official Playwright CDPSession/browser launch and Chromium Tracing/Profiler API documentation before implementing the harness. Use documented public APIs only. An existing executable/package can be used read-only; if a dependency is needed, install it in the private artifact workspace, never package.json/lockfile or shared/tmp. No elevation, kernel setting change, browser sandbox removal invented for this task, process suspension or relaunch loop. If launch/access is unsupported, report that exact limit and stop.

Tracing may be process-wide **only because the entire launched process is exclusively yours**. Start/stop/export through the supported CDP interface; close it normally through its owner on completion. No browser/server may survive handoff. Do not copy user profiles or collect unrelated process command lines. All traces must identify their own browser/version/flags, geometry quality and candidate. This environment is not the earlier shared-preview trial; a faster sample here cannot erase its misses or become a controlled speedup claim.

## Precise capability gate

Before game timing, on an owned local synthetic page prove a named marker/frame→renderer PID/main TID mapping, correlated monotonic wall/thread timestamps and useful clock precision over bounded known busy and idle intervals. Inspect supported event categories. Capture sampled JS stacks and GC/JIT events with matching source information, and quantify dropped events/observer cost. API units do not prove precision. Keep this a finite capability test, not a benchmark loop.

Root refines the previous all-facilities preflight: **reliable main-thread execution attribution can justify a CPU-work correction even if kernel scheduler tracing is unavailable**. Explicitly measure the residual and uncertainty; off-CPU time alone cannot distinguish runqueue wait from native/driver blocking. `/proc` scheduler counters, if read, must belong only to the verified owned target and have measured bracket uncertainty. No process totals, pressure average or quantized per-call clock substitutes for attribution. A source/VM cost must actually dominate a slow interval before a production change is proposed. If timing remains largely unexplained, stop inconclusive. This narrower causal question changes no50 ms acceptance predicate and grants no external-noise waiver.
